w5.trans_en: Mother is the third daughter; both older sisters have already passed away.
w5.point_en: Sibling order: 長男／長女 → 次男／次女 → 三男／三女. The youngest is 末っ子. Here “two older sisters” tells you the rank.
why_en: 一人っ子 = only child, so there would be no older sisters.
一人娘 = only daughter — same contradiction.
長女 = eldest daughter, so she cannot have older sisters.
三女 = third daughter, so two older sisters is exactly right.

w5.trans_en: As you get older, your hair gradually falls out.
w5.point_en: 抜ける is for something that used to grow on the body falling out — 髪の毛が抜ける, 歯が抜ける. The opposite is 生える, tested in Q7.
why_en: かれる = 枯れる, plants wither; not used for hair.
ちる = 散る, petals fall.
ぬける = 抜ける, hair or teeth fall out. Correct.
くさる = 腐る, food goes bad.

w5.trans_en: “I’ll be leaving shortly, so please don’t go to any trouble.”
w5.point_en: Watch who says the set phrase: おかまいなく is guest to host; ご遠慮なく is host to guest.
why_en: おかまいなく = don’t fuss over me. Correct.
ご遠慮なく = please help yourself — said by the host, so the direction is reversed.
お気の毒に = sympathy for someone unlucky.
お大事に = take care, said to someone who is ill.

w5.trans_en: When he was little, our son was a sweet child who listened to his parents.
w5.point_en: 素直 is accepting without talking back. 正直 is not lying. Both can look like “honest” in Chinese, but they split in Japanese.
why_en: スマートに = slim / slick — not “obedient.”
すなおに = 素直に, without fuss. Correct.
いいかげんに = sloppily — the opposite.
正直に = honestly (not lying), not the same as “obedient.”

w5.trans_en: I spilled hot water and burned my foot.
w5.point_en: やけど is specifically a burn or scald: やけどをする. Ordinary injuries are けがをする.
why_en: うがい = gargling.
けが = a knock or cut; burns have their own word.
くせ = a habit.
やけど = a burn / scald. Correct.

w5.trans_en: I ate too much and my stomach hurts.
w5.point_en: Body part ＋ が痛い is the usual “it hurts” pattern: 胃が痛い, 頭が痛い.
why_en: 腰 = lower back.
胃 = stomach — what hurts after overeating. Correct.
頭 = head.
肩 = shoulder.

w5.trans_en: Our junior-high son has started growing a beard.
w5.point_en: 生える = grow out; 抜ける = fall out. ひげが生える, 歯が生える, かびが生える.
why_en: はえて = 生えて, hair/teeth/mold growing. Correct.
はげて = going bald.
ぬけて = falling out — opposite direction.
たまって = piling up.

w5.trans_en: He’s stingy, so he’s never treated me even once.
w5.point_en: けち is a personality that hates spending. Being actually poor is 貧乏.
why_en: けちだ = stingy. Correct.
しつこい = persistent / greasy.
だらしない = sloppy.
苦しい = hard up — money trouble, not character.

w5.trans_en: Looking at old photos, I remember that pure feeling from childhood.
w5.point_en: A na-adjective needs な before a noun. Option 2 is a dictionary-form verb; it would have to be 落ち着いた気持ち.
why_en: ハンサムな = handsome (of a man), not a feeling.
落ち着く = verb; you’d need 落ち着いた気持ち.
かしこい = clever — odd with 気持ち.
純粋な = pure. Correct.

w5.trans_en: Working so late — thank you for your hard work.
w5.point_en: ごくろうさま is basically from a superior to a junior. お疲れさま is safer toward a boss.
why_en: ごくろうさまです = thanks for the work. Correct.
とんでもないです = not at all — a humble reply to praise.
お先に失礼します = I’ll leave first.
おじゃまします = excuse me for coming in.

w5.trans_en: (Definition) So bright you can hardly look.
w5.point_en: まぶしい is light so strong you can’t keep your eyes open.
why_en: つらい = painful.
まぶしい = dazzling. Correct.
くだらない = worthless.
かしこい = clever.

w5.trans_en: (Definition) Someone who deliberately makes trouble or does things people dislike.
w5.point_en: The key is わざと (on purpose). Only 意地悪 includes meaning to make the other person suffer.
why_en: いじわるな人 = mean on purpose. Correct.
だらしない人 = sloppy.
いいかげんな人 = careless.
無責任な人 = irresponsible. 3 and 4 are “not serious,” not “mean on purpose.”

w5.trans_en: (Definition) Having been out of touch for a long time.
w5.point_en: ご無沙汰しています is the polite “long time no contact,” more formal than 久しぶり.
why_en: おきのどく = sympathy.
ご遠慮 = holding back / declining.
ごぶさた = ご無沙汰. Correct.
おすまい = someone’s home.

w5.trans_en: (Definition) Someone who takes the initiative.
w5.point_en: 積極的 vs 消極的. Don’t mix it with ずうずうしい (shamelessly pushy) — that is negative.
why_en: のんきな人 = easygoing.
おちついている人 = calm.
積極的な人 = proactive. Correct.
ずうずうしい人 = thick-skinned.

w5.trans_en: (Definition) Food and the like going bad after sitting too long.
w5.point_en: All four mean “go bad,” but the object differs: food 腐る, plants 枯れる, shape 崩れる, flowers 散る.
why_en: くさる = 腐る, food spoils. Correct.
かれる = 枯れる, plants wither.
くずれる = 崩れる, a shape collapses.
ちる = 散る, flowers fall.

w5.trans_en: The car in front was too slow, so I passed it.
w5.point_en: のろい = 遅い, but with annoyance — “poky.”
why_en: スピードを出しすぎる = going too fast — opposite.
じゃまな = in the way, not “slow.”
おそい = slow. Correct.
ブレーキをかけない = not braking.

w5.trans_en: “Don’t rub your eyes with dirty hands.”
w5.point_en: こする is rubbing back and forth; かく is scratching with nails. 〜ちゃ is spoken 〜ては.
why_en: かんじゃ = bite.
はいちゃ = put on (shoes).
そめちゃ = dye.
かいちゃ = 掻いちゃ, scratch — closest to こする. Correct.

w5.trans_en: “Please have a seat.”
w5.point_en: かける here is “sit.” Honorific おかけになる = お座りになる.
why_en: すわって = sit. Correct.
食べて = eat (召し上がる).
飲んで = drink.
入って = come in.

w5.trans_en: I wrote random answers on the test.
w5.point_en: でたらめ is making things up with no basis; いいかげん is doing a sloppy job. Both are “not taking it seriously.”
why_en: いいかげんな = sloppy — closest to でたらめ. Correct.
くだらない = worthless.
うそつきの = a liar — describes a person, not answers.
なだらかな = a gentle slope.

w5.trans_en: The cold isn’t serious, so I’ll go out as planned.
w5.point_en: 大したことがない = not that serious, often of illness or injury.
why_en: ずうずうしくない = not pushy.
だらしない = sloppy.
たいしたことがない = nothing major. Correct.
しつこくない = not persistent.

w5.trans_en: He always says unreliable things, so you can’t trust him.
w5.point_en: いいかげん describes an attitude toward work or speech, not looks or manners themselves.
why_en: Odd with clothes — sloppy clothes are だらしない服.
Sitting quietly is おとなしい.
礼儀 takes 礼儀正しい／知らない, not いいかげんな礼儀.
Irresponsible talk you can’t trust. Correct.

w5.trans_en: My brother always takes the bigger piece of cake — so unfair.
w5.point_en: ずるい is using an unfair method to get an advantage — a complaint about someone.
why_en: Coming home late is annoying, not “cheating.”
Busy looking after a brother isn’t sneaky.
Always taking the big piece = looking after himself. Correct.
Lending me everything is kind, not ずるい.

w5.trans_en: Only a slim person could wear this outfit.
w5.point_en: Japanese スマート is a slim figure or a slick method — not English smart “clever.” A classic 和製英語 trap.
why_en: スマートな人 = a slim person. Correct.
Ability is 能力のある; スマート does not mean clever here.
Hair is not スマート.
A rich life is 豊かな生活.

w5.trans_en: I’ve gotten into the bad habit of not being able to sleep without a drink.
w5.point_en: くせ is a personal habit, often negative: くせがつく. Social customs are 習慣.
why_en: Sneezing and itchy eyes are 症状 of hay fever, not くせ.
Year-end gifts are a 習慣.
A scar from surgery is 傷あと.
Can’t sleep without a drink = a (bad) habit. Correct.

w5.trans_en: My son only watches worthless TV and doesn’t study.
w5.point_en: くだらない = worthless, usually of content (talk, shows, books), not to praise a person or an object’s performance.
why_en: くだらない人 clashes with “liked by everyone.”
A house not collapsing is 倒れない.
A sharp knife is よく切れる.
くだらないテレビ = worthless TV. Correct.

w6.trans_en: It took a long time, but the report is finally finished.
w6.point_en: ついに stresses a result after a long process, close to とうとう.
why_en: とたんに is 〜たとたん — the instant of an action; it can’t stand alone like this.
ついに = at last after a long process. Correct.
そろそろ = it’s about time — something about to happen.
すっきり = refreshed — not “finished.”

w6.trans_en: The TV picture suddenly disappeared.
w6.point_en: 突然 = 急に, with no warning. Q15’s いきなり is the same idea, more spoken.
why_en: ふと = on a whim / by chance.
しっかり = firmly / properly.
とつぜん = suddenly. Correct.
やっと = only just, after effort.

w6.trans_en: I put in new batteries, but I still can’t hear the radio clearly.
w6.point_en: This set tests 取り替える／取り出す／飛び出す together (Q3, 9, 10). Don’t mix them.
why_en: 取り込んだ = take in (laundry).
取り替えた = replace old with new. Correct.
取り出した = take out from inside — Q9.
取り入れた = adopt.

w6.trans_en: The cat is wandering around the house.
w6.point_en: うろうろ has a restless “don’t know where to go” feel; ぶらぶら is an easy stroll — opposite mood.
why_en: うろうろ = wander aimlessly. Correct.
ぶつぶつ = mutter.
ぶらぶら = stroll at ease.
のんびり = take it easy — Q12.

w6.trans_en: I think I have a cold. I’m not coughing much, but my throat hurts.
w6.point_en: 咳が出る is a set phrase, like 熱が出る and 鼻水が出る.
why_en: つけない — 咳をつける is not a phrase.
かからない — 風邪にかかる is catching a cold, not with 咳.
たたない — no collocation.
出ない = the negative of 咳が出る. Correct.

w6.trans_en: As soon as I get home I turn the computer on first.
w6.point_en: まず is the first step in order, close to 最初に.
why_en: ぜひ = by all means — needs a wish or request.
どうか = please (pleading).
まず = first of all. Correct.
結局 = in the end.

w6.trans_en: I slept well, so I woke up feeling refreshed this morning.
w6.point_en: すっきり is the ease after tiredness or worry is gone. Q11 tests its other sense: uncluttered.
why_en: さっぱり = fresh after washing / さっぱり〜ない.
とうとう = finally.
すっきり = clear-headed after sleep. Correct.
かなり = quite.

w6.trans_en: I called the company to ask; they said the person in charge is off and they don’t really know.
w6.point_en: 問い合わせる is asking a company or office for information. Q25 tests the same verb.
why_en: 話しかけたら = spoke to someone.
申し込んだら = applied.
受け付けたら = accepted (the receiving side).
問い合わせたら = inquired. Correct.

w6.trans_en: I took my wallet out of my pocket.
w6.point_en: 取り出す is a person taking something out of a container. 飛び出す is something bursting out on its own.
why_en: 取り出した = took out. Correct.
飛び出した = burst out — Q10.
取りかえた = replaced — Q3.
受け取った = received.

w6.trans_en: A child ran out in front of the car.
w6.point_en: 飛び出す = dash out suddenly. Common on traffic signs: 子どもの飛び出しに注意.
why_en: 飛びかかって = leap at (to attack).
飛び出して = dash out. Correct.
飛び入れて is not a word.
飛びすぎて = fly too far.

w6.trans_en: (Definition) Comfortable because nothing is in the way.
w6.point_en: All four are っ＋り adverbs; you have to split them by meaning. Q7 is the other sense of すっきり.
why_en: やっぱり = as expected.
すっかり = completely.
すっきり = neat / uncluttered. Correct.
がっかり = disappointed.

w6.trans_en: (Definition) Resting in a leisurely way.
w6.point_en: のんびり is unhurried and relaxed: のんびり暮らす.
why_en: はっきり = clearly.
さっぱり = refreshed / not at all.
しっかり = firmly.
のんびり = at ease. Correct.

w6.trans_en: (Definition) Doing something while thinking “I’ll do it this way.”
w6.point_en: わざと vs うっかり (by accident). Don’t mix with わざわざ (going out of your way).
why_en: ふと = without meaning to — opposite.
きちんと = neatly / properly.
わざと = on purpose. Correct.
じっと = without moving.

w6.trans_en: (Definition) Restless because things aren’t going your way.
w6.point_en: いらいら is irritation when things stall. どきどき is heartbeat; うろうろ is a physical wander.
why_en: ぶつぶつ = mutter.
いらいら = irritated. Correct.
どきどき = heart pounding.
うろうろ = wander — Q4.

w6.trans_en: (Definition) Something that happens all of a sudden.
w6.point_en: いきなり is the same as Q2’s 突然, just more spoken.
why_en: いきなり = all of a sudden. Correct.
たいてい = usually — Q24.
ますます = more and more.
いっぺんに = all at once.

w6.trans_en: A: “Can you cook?” B: “Yes, I do sometimes.”
w6.point_en: Frequency low to high: ぜんぜん ＜ たまに／ときどき ＜ よく ＜ たいてい ＜ いつも. Q24 is たいてい.
why_en: たまに = occasionally — closest to ときどき. Correct.
たいてい = most of the time — much more often.
けっこう = quite.
ちゃんと = properly.

w6.trans_en: My daughter got into university, so I can relax.
w6.point_en: ほっとする = 安心する — a sigh of relief after a worry is gone.
why_en: そっとした — そっと is “gently,” not relief.
ほっとした = relieved. Correct.
のんびりした = leisurely.
ぼんやりした = vacant / vague.

w6.trans_en: I was so nervous at the interview that I couldn’t answer well.
w6.point_en: あがる also means stage fright: 人前であがる.
why_en: 言いなおして = say it again.
落ち着いて = calm — opposite.
急いで = in a hurry.
あがって = freeze in front of people. Correct.

w6.trans_en: Let’s mark the questions we got wrong.
w6.point_en: 印をつける is a set phrase; the verb has to be つける.
why_en: かけて — no collocation.
おいて — no collocation.
あげて — no collocation.
つけて = 印をつける. Correct.

w6.trans_en: We leave first thing tomorrow morning.
w6.point_en: たつ written 発つ is “depart.” 立つ (stand up) is a different word — 席を立つ in week 6 day 6.
why_en: たちます = 発つ, set out. Correct.
つけます — no collocation.
ききます — no collocation.
いれます — no collocation.

w6.trans_en: She speaks French fluently.
w6.point_en: ぺらぺら is specifically fluent in a foreign language. The distractors each have their own mimetic.
why_en: Fluent answering is すらすらと答える.
Complaining is ぶつぶつ文句を言う.
フランス語がぺらぺら = fluent in a language. Correct.
Hungry is おなかがぺこぺこ.

w6.trans_en: The ring is sparkling.
w6.point_en: ぴかぴか is shining or polished (new or just cleaned). Not used for how the body or mood feels.
why_en: 指輪がぴかぴか光る = sparkle. Correct.
A clean bath can be ぴかぴか, but “feeling good after a bath” is not.
A mess is ぐちゃぐちゃ.
Waiting for results is どきどき.

w6.trans_en: I asked someone who happened to be passing for directions.
w6.point_en: 通りかかる is passing by chance. Intentionally dropping in is 立ち寄る; going past is 通り過ぎる — all three are in the options.
why_en: Getting into university is やっと大学に合格しました.
Stopping at a restaurant is 立ち寄った.
Going through a park is 通り過ぎると.
通りかかった人 = someone who happened to pass. Correct.

w6.trans_en: On days off I usually stay home.
w6.point_en: たいてい is high frequency (most cases), not degree. Q16’s たまに is the opposite end.
why_en: 〜こともあります wants たまに.
A computer dying suddenly is いきなり／とつぜん.
休日はたいてい家にいます = most days off at home. Correct.
Farther than expected is ずいぶん遠かった.

w6.trans_en: I asked the travel agency for the detailed schedule.
w6.point_en: 問い合わせる is asking a company. 待ち合わせる (meet up) differs by one character.
why_en: Changing batteries is 取り替える — Q3.
Checking answers is 見直す.
Meeting a client in front of the station is 待ち合わせた.
旅行会社に問い合わせた = inquired. Correct.
